translit: uvācha pārtha paśhyaitān samavetān kurūn iti
theme: Krishna Says: Look at Them Carefully
hindi: भीष्म, द्रोणाचार्य और सभी राजाओं के ठीक सामने रथ खड़ा करके श्रीकृष्ण ने कहा, “हे पार्थ, यहाँ इकट्ठे हुए इन कुरुवंशियों को देखो।”
english: Right in front of Bhishma, Drona and all the kings, Krishna said, “Partha, look at all these Kurus gathered here.”
deeper: Krishna did not park the chariot just anywhere. He stopped it facing Bhishma and Drona, the grandfather and the teacher whom Arjuna loved and respected the most. Arjuna had asked to see who he would have to fight (1.22). Krishna simply let him see the real answer.

Notice the word “Kurus”. Krishna did not say “enemies” or “the wicked ones”. He said Kurus, the family. By saying only “look”, Krishna did not push Arjuna toward any feeling. He let Arjuna see the whole truth with his own eyes: these are people he knows, loves and is related to.

Krishna also calls him Partha, “son of Pritha”, which is another name for his mother Kunti. It is a gentle, loving way of speaking. A good guide often opens our eyes first and lets us feel and think for ourselves. Seeing clearly comes before deciding wisely.
words: Bhishma, the grand and respected elder of the Kuru family
Drona, the teacher of the Kuru princes
in front of, in the presence of
of the kings, the rulers of the earth
the Kurus, members of the Kuru family
thus (marks the end of what was said)
background: Arjuna, the great archer, was ready for battle on his chariot. He asked Krishna to stop the chariot between the two armies so that he could see who stood ready to fight (1.22) and who had come to take the side of Duryodhana (1.23).

Sanjaya then told King Dhritarashtra that Krishna, the Lord of the senses, drew the finest chariot right between the two armies (1.24). In this verse Krishna places it in front of Bhishma and Drona and asks Arjuna to look.
lessons: Before a big decision, stop and see clearly who and what is really in front of you.
A good guide opens your eyes
Krishna did not lecture Arjuna here; he helped Arjuna see the truth for himself.
Real people stand behind every problem
Behind every conflict are people we know, and they deserve to be seen as people.
Respect for elders is part of seeing
Arjuna was placed in front of Bhishma and Drona, and his heart naturally stirred with respect.
It is not easy to look at what troubles us, but we cannot solve what we refuse to see.
examples: Riya looks at the whole question paper before writing anything. She sees which questions are easy and which are hard, and then plans her time.
Aman has to pick teams in the colony. He first looks at all his friends properly, including his cousin, and then decides fairly instead of rushing.
After a fight, Meena looks at her best friend Kavya from across the room. She realises it is not an enemy there, but a friend she loves, and her anger softens.
Before complaining about dinner, Rohan looks at everything his mother has cooked with so much love. He decides to try it all.
Tara notices her grandfather has been walking slowly lately. When she really looks at him, she understands why he needs her help with the stairs.
Imran stops at the edge of the road and looks carefully both ways. A clear look keeps him safe.
Pooja is afraid to start cleaning her room. When she finally looks at everything on the floor, she sees it is just a few piles, and she begins.
Karthik broke a neighbour’s flower pot. He walks over, looks at the pot and Mrs. Iyer’s face, and says sorry instead of hiding.

story.title: Arjuna and the Bird’s Eye
paras: When the Kuru princes were young, their teacher Drona wanted to test their focus. He hung a wooden bird on a tall tree and asked each prince to aim at its eye.

Before each turn, Drona asked, “What do you see?” One prince said, “I see the tree, the branches and the bird.” Drona shook his head and asked him to step aside. Others said they saw their brothers, the leaves and the sky.
When Arjuna’s turn came, he replied calmly, “I see only the eye of the bird.” Drona smiled, and Arjuna’s arrow flew straight to the mark.

Years later on the battlefield, Arjuna’s eyes were again asked to see, but this time Krishna asked him to see the whole picture: the elders, the teachers, the kings. A clear look sometimes means focusing on one thing, and sometimes it means seeing everything honestly.
story.moral: Lesson: Look carefully and honestly, both at the one thing that matters and at the whole picture, before you act.

quiz.q: Whom did Krishna place the chariot in front of?
quiz.x: Krishna stopped the chariot in front of Bhishma, Drona and the kings.

quiz.q: What did Krishna ask Arjuna to do?
quiz.x: Krishna said, “Partha, behold these Kurus assembled.”

quiz.q: Why is it meaningful that Krishna said “Kurus” and not “enemies”?
o: He wanted Arjuna to see them as his own family
He wanted to hide the truth
quiz.x: The word Kurus reminds Arjuna that these are his own relatives and elders.

quiz.q: What does the verse teach about decisions?
quiz.x: Krishna lets Arjuna see the truth first, which is the base of a wise decision.

reel.hook: What if Krishna made Arjuna look at his own family first?
reel.lesson: See clearly and honestly before you decide, because real people stand behind every problem.
reel.caption:
Krishna did not tell Arjuna what to feel. He just said, “Look.” 👀
When we pause and really see the people in front of us, wiser choices follow. 🙏
